metas.name: Austria - bus stop sign
metas.note:
Austrian bus stop signs contain a yellow and green circle with the letter H.

NOTE: This design is relatively unique in Europe. The only other country with similar bus stop signs is Germany.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Belgium  - Flanders and Brussels bus stop signs
metas.note: Bus stop signs in Flanders (and Brussels) have a white rectangle at the top. In Wallonia they will have a yellow top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Belgium  - Wallonia bus stop sign
metas.note: Bus stop signs in Flanders (and Brussels) have a white rectangle at the top. In Wallonia they will have a yellow top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Estonia - bus stop sign
metas.note:
Estonian bus stop signs have this design.

The bus has four windows. This is mostly useful to distinguish it from the Latvian bus stop sign, which has five windows.

Note, however, that Lithuania has the same bus stop signs as Estonia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Finland - bus stop sign
metas.note:
Finland has two styles of bus stop signs, a blue and white one, and a yellow and black one.

NOTE: This can be used to tell Finland apart from Sweden, which has many different bus stop signs, most of which have the names of the stops on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/finland.

metas.name: Germany  - Berlin bus stop signs
metas.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Germany  - Bremen bus stop sign
metas.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Germany  - Bremerhaven bus stop sign
metas.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Germany  - Hamburg bus stop signs
metas.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Germany standard - standard German bus stop signs
metas.note: Like Austria, Germany uses a wide variety of regional bus stops, all of which have the big yellow and green H symbol on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Ireland (new) - Ireland new bus top signs
metas.note: In the most recent rounds of coverage you’ll find green-and-yellow TFI (Transport for Ireland) bus stop signs, whereas in older coverage you’ll predominantly see Bus Éireann signs.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland (old) - Ireland old bus stop signs
metas.note: In the most recent rounds of coverage you’ll find green-and-yellow TFI (Transport for Ireland) bus stop signs, whereas in older coverage you’ll predominantly see Bus Éireann signs.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Latvia bus stop sign
metas.note:
Latvian bus stop signs have this design.

Most importantly, the bus has five windows. Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia. The other two Baltic countries have four windows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/latvia.

metas.name: Liechtenstein  - Balzers bus stop sign
metas.note:
Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Balzers sometimes uses black bus stop signs.

NOTE: Regular bus stops are also present.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/liechtenstein.

metas.name: Liechtenstein  - Vaduz bus stop sign
metas.note:
Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Vaduz sometimes uses red bus stop signs.

NOTE: Regular bus stops are also present.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/liechtenstein.

metas.name: Liechtenstein standard - standard Liechtenstein bus stop sign
metas.note:
Bus stops in Liechtenstein use a green-and-white design, with a black metallic border around the sign. The phrase LIEMOBIL is written at the top.

NOTE: The metallic frame is not always black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Lithuania - bus stop sign
metas.note:
Lithuanian bus stop signs have this design.

The bus has four windows. This is mostly useful to distinguish it from the Latvian bus stop sign, which has five windows.

Note however, that Estonia has the same bus stop signs as Lithuania.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lithuania.

metas.name: Luxembourg - bus stop sign
metas.note:
Bus stop signs are blue and always have this exact design. The bus has six windows.

NOTE: Bus stop signs in Belgium and the Netherlands have significantly different designs. For example, the Belgian bus stop sign always has a yellow signpost.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.
